newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse activity improves, index down.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse activity improves, index down.

text.p: Mixed signals were seen at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Tuesday as activity picked up but the market was on average still depressed, brokers and bourse officials said.
The 20-share index lost 10.44 points to stand at 3007.67.
Turnover was posted at 11.685 million shillings traded on 326,448 shares from 7.652 million shillings traded on 226,754 shares on Monday.
Bourse officials said the market was buoyant with many small lots traded; 24,970 shares of Barclays Bank traded at 97 unchanged and 80,175 shares of National Bank of Kenya traded at 14.70 from 14.50.
Some 58,070 shares of Kenya Airways at 9.20 and 32,265 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank traded at 57 also helped boost the market turnover.

"It's hard to tell exactly which way the market is going. Institutional investors appear to have pulled out from the market for now, but many small investors are offloading their shares," a broker said.
He said lack of participation by institutional investors had reduced demand for shares, pulling prices down.
"There was increased participation by foreigners in the market, which could have been another reason why turnover was up," another broker said.

Foreign investors continued to dominate buying in Firestone East Africa with 19,000 shares at 24.55. In Uchumi Supermarket they bought 29,500 shares at 46, and 6,400 shares of National Industrial Credit at 40.55 and 40.50.
"Foreign investors are simply taking advantage of the current prices in the market which are trading at a discount," one broker said.

A senior broker said the market might be getting out of a bearish mood: "The prices have been down for so long that most investors are now thinking they can't possibly go lower. At this point I think the only way forward is up, but it's still too early to tell," he added.
